rationale: Direct evidence from Muelas et al. (2026) documents the first described family with adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy carrying compound heterozygous variants (p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr). In this adult-onset sibship, one of the two affected siblings was explicitly confirmed on brain MRI to have asymptomatic (subclinical) cerebellar atrophy without overt clinical ataxia. Furthermore, broader phenotypic descriptions across the literature (Liewluck 2025, Okubo et al. 2026) demonstrate that cerebellar pathology is an allelic feature of SNUPN disruption, ranging from subclinical structural atrophy to full spinocerebellar degeneration, confirming that structural cerebellar atrophy can indeed occur subclinically in adult-onset muscular dystrophy.

evidence.text: In a family presenting with adult-onset SNUPN-related muscular dystrophy (LGMDR29) caused by p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr variants, systematic neurological and neuroimaging assessment revealed that one of the affected siblings had asymptomatic cerebellar atrophy on brain MRI.

evidence.text: Pediatric cohorts of SNUPN deficiency present with childhood-onset muscular dystrophy, multi-system features, and overt developmental or neurological defects, indicating that subclinical presentation of cerebellar findings is characteristic of later adult-onset presentations rather than severe infantile/childhood presentations.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of adult-onset vs. childhood-onset LGMDR29 patients display subclinical structural cerebellar atrophy when systematically screened by volumetric brain MRI?
new_directions.rationale: Brain imaging has historically been omitted in patients presenting with purely myopathic signs; prospective volumetric cerebellar MRI across adult and pediatric cohorts will clarify the true penetrance and timeline of cerebellar volume loss.

new_directions.question_text: Do specific missense variants in the N-terminal or central regions of SNUPN (such as p.Arg27Cys and p.Cys174Tyr) spare cerebellar Purkinje cell integrity compared to C-terminal cluster variants?
new_directions.rationale: Adult-onset myopathy cases with subclinical atrophy carry N-terminal/central variants, whereas classical spinocerebellar atrophy or severe congenital multi-system presentations may correlate with differing impacts on importin-beta binding and Cajal body integrity.
